conventions.bbox: [x0, y0, x1, y1], fractions of the PDF page (A4, incl. the white frame around the scan)

drawings.description: à gauche de la note, un croquis : le cercle unité dans le plan, avec les deux axes ; un point $\zeta$ sur le cercle, relié à l'origine ; la verticale passant par $\zeta$, épaissie, qui coupe l'axe horizontal à l'abscisse marquée $\frac{1}{2}$.
drawings.kind: unit circle with the point zeta = exp(2 i pi/6) above the abscissa 1/2
drawings.notes: As on the page: the two axes through the origin, the circle (an ellipse fitted to his outline), the point zeta on it in the first quadrant, the segment from the origin to zeta, the heavy vertical line through zeta, from above the circle down to the horizontal axis, and the labels zeta (right of the point) and 1/2 (under the axis, at the foot of the vertical). The origin, the point and the foot of the vertical are computed once and all strokes drawn through them. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: moitié gauche de la page, en haut : une sphère avec son équateur et deux méridiens ; au pôle, un gros point d'où partent des traits épais descendant vers la gauche le long de la sphère ; sur l'équateur, des points marqués, avec une flèche le long de l'arc avant (vers la droite) et une flèche le long de l'arc arrière (vers la gauche).
drawings.kind: sphere with equator, meridians and arrows at the pole and along the equator
drawings.notes: The outline (an ellipse fitted to his several strokes), the equator as a back arc and a front arc, the heavy meridian from the pole down to the left point of the front arc, a second thin meridian in the middle, the heavy point at the pole, the marked points on the equator (one at the foot of the heavy meridian, one in the middle of the back arc, three on the right part of the front arc, the last beyond the outline), the arrow along the front arc pointing right from the foot of the meridian, and the arrow along the back arc pointing left. Left out: the ink scribble round the pole (several heavy strokes going down to the left, gone over many times; drawn as one heavy stroke along the meridian), the long line through the pole which belongs to the oblique line crossing the sheet. Still differs: the strokes at the pole (the note of the transcription sees arrows tangent to the sphere there) are too blotted to tell their number or heads. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: moitié gauche de la page, plus bas : un faisceau de cinq courbes issues d'un même point d'une droite, qui s'ouvrent vers la droite et se rejoignent au bord droit de la page.
drawings.kind: bundle of curves from one point, meeting again at the right
drawings.notes: The short line through the base point at the left, and five curves from that point which open out and come together again at the right edge of the sheet, all drawn from the one base point to the one end point; one of them has a step (a short steep rise) in its middle, as on the page. Left out: the two long oblique lines that cross the sheet (they run through the sphere above and separate parts of the page), and all the labels round the bundle, which the transcription gives (V(omega), phi_omega(R_K), P_i, t_omega ...). Still differs: the curves run close together and cross; their courses between the two ends are a reading, and the count of five follows the note of the transcription (four or five can be told apart). Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: à gauche des premières lignes, un cercle portant trois petits traits (repères), en haut, en bas à gauche et en bas à droite ; à gauche du repère inférieur gauche, la lettre « $e$ ».
drawings.kind: circle with three marks, one labelled e
drawings.notes: As on the page: the circle and three short marks across it, at the top, at the lower left and at the lower right (the two lower ones heavier), each drawn radially at the direction where he put it; the letter e, followed by a dot, at the left of the lower left mark. The three marks are roughly a third of a turn apart. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.
